tasks.title: Separate global theme from operator surface personality
tasks.risk: The application reports dark theme while mw-platform overrides its tokens and remains visually light.
acceptance_criteria: Theme light, dark, and system apply coherently to every application surface.
Operator/editorial surface personality is represented independently from color theme.
Sidebar, header, cards, controls, semantic statuses, overlays, and focus states change consistently without theme leakage.
evidence_required: light and dark screenshots for dashboard, case, and platform

tasks.title: Migrate specimen-based consumers to semantic primitives and define screen asset mapping
tasks.risk: Full specimen artwork is currently scaled into icon slots and image-based labels can diverge from runtime semantics and accessibility text.
acceptance_criteria: ProvenanceRail, status, graph, evidence, and legal consumers use atomic primitives or semantic HTML rather than specimen cards.
Status labels are data-driven HTML and remain synchronized with accessible names.
Every production screen declares allowed and required asset families by semantic purpose.
Dashboard includes bounded evidence-specific visualizations that improve decision making without decorative noise.
evidence_required: component tests for label and state synchronization

tasks.title: Establish full visual regression, breakpoint, theme, and zoom coverage
tasks.risk: Current browser QA covers only landing and dashboard at 390 and 1440 pixels and has no stable visual snapshots.
acceptance_criteria: Visual baselines cover landing, dashboard, case, correlation, auth, and platform in light and dark modes.
Responsive tests cover 390, 640, 768, 1024, and 1440 pixels plus relevant breakpoint boundaries.
Tests cover 200 percent zoom, reduced motion, high contrast, long content, asset fallback, and horizontal overflow.
CI publishes diffs on failure without accepting new baselines automatically.
